title: feat(spec): the liveness gate reads the retiredKey() tombstone marker — a tombstoned key may not be graded live
body:
Fixes #19062

Clause-②: no

## What this closes

The liveness gate graded a schema property from two sources: the ledger row's `status`, or — with no row — a `[experimental` / `[planned` marker read by `markerStatus()`. It had **no reading of the `retiredKey()` tombstone marker at all**, so `tombstone + status: live` was a *structurally permitted* combination rather than an oversight:

- the forward pass is satisfied — a tombstone keeps the key in the walked shape, so the row exists and is classified;
- the orphan pass is satisfied for the same reason — the property has not left the schema;
- nothing constrained what that row was allowed to **say**.

This adds the join both directions lacked, as a fourth direction beside the orphan scan: walk the tombstones the gate already reaches, and ask each one's ledger row what it claims.

## Ordering — discharged

This section used to read "this PR must not merge before #19059", and that constraint is now **spent**: #19059 landed as `a362e0e425`, `main` is merged into this branch, and the single offending row it named — `agent/tools`, #18304's — is `dead` on the real ledgers. Re-measured by the seat on this PR's head `3d49d7a199` (2026-09-18T22:08Z):

- `check:liveness` against the shipped ledgers: **exit 0**, printing `79 graded with a status the tombstone allows`.
- The 16 control cases that were red for that one cause are green. The whole `scripts/liveness/` suite: **333 passed (333)** over 12 files, exit 0.

⛔ No landing order remains on this PR. Read the population table below as the measurement that *motivated* the rule, not as a description of today's tree.

## The population, measured — the card's first deliverable

The card states its own evidence limit: "the population is unmeasured, and measuring it is the first piece of the work — it needs exactly the join the gate lacks". Measured over all 39 governed types by the gate's own walk, at two commits — the tree the rule was written against, and this PR's head `3d49d7a199` (the right-hand column re-measured by the seat, 2026-09-18T22:08Z):

| reading | tree the rule was written against | this PR's head |
|---|---|---|
| `[REMOVED]` tombstones the gate's walk reaches | **79** | **79** |
| …graded `dead` | **78** | **79** |
| …graded `live` (the defective state) | **1** — `agent/tools` | **0** — #19059 repaired that row |
| …whose status came from an explicit ledger row | **79 / 79** | **79 / 79** (none from a marker, none from `childrenDefault`, none UNCLASSIFIED) |

The full list of 79 is in the report on the card. **Drift control on the instrument**: the census walk reproduces the gate's own per-type verdict counts for all 39 types and 1092 verdict points exactly (compared against `check:liveness --json`'s `classified + unclassified`), so it is the gate's walk and not a copy of it.

**Reachable radius of that census** — it is the gate's walk, so it is the ledger-driven drill, nothing wider. **Known targets necessarily outside it**: a full-depth walk of the same governed roots finds **59 further `[REMOVED]` tombstones the gate never reaches** — `object/fields.conditionalRequired`, `object/listViews.performance`, `job/retryPolicy.retryDelayMs` among them — because they sit under containers carrying a blanket verdict (the 601 child keys the gate already reports as classified nowhere). No rule placed in this gate can grade a key the gate does not walk; closing that is the undrilled-container worklist, not this card.

## Why remedy (2), measured rather than argued

Triage named two shapes and refused to pick. Their side-effect surfaces were measured, each applied alone to the base gate with the mutation proven on disk before any verdict was read:

- **(1) a third `[REMOVED]` arm in `markerStatus()`** — on the acceptance sample this leaves the gate at **exit 0**. `markerStatus()` is consulted only when `led?.status` is falsy, and all 79 tombstones the walk reaches take their status from an explicit row, so this arm changes the verdict of **0 of the 79** today. What it does change is the no-row case, which the gate currently reports as UNCLASSIFIED and fails on, and which `ORPHAN_GUIDANCE` tells authors never to create — so (1) alone would *silence* an existing loud failure. It cannot satisfy the acceptance.
- **(2) a rule beside the tombstone-row rule** — implemented here. The forbidden set is a named constant holding exactly `live`, which is what was ruled. `planned` / `experimental` / `live-elsewhere` on a tombstone are equally false, and their population today is zero, so widening the set is a separate measurement rather than a rider on this one.

## Acceptance

Every leg runs the real gate the way CI invokes it, via `--ledger-root` against a copied ledger.

The carrier the legs flip is **derived per run from the gate's own `report.tombstones` enumeration**, not named: top-level, not a `BOUND_PROOF_PATHS` coordinate, and currently `dead`. A fixture pinned to one row's *current verdict* is pinned to a moving fact, which is how this block first broke — it named `agent/tools`, that row went `dead` upstream, and the "this would be a no-op" guard took four cases red. The seat re-derived the same filter chain independently (2026-09-18T22:08Z): **79 enumerated → 42 top-level → 42 unbound → 42 `dead`**, carrier `action/bulkEnabled`. ⚠️ Today only the top-level filter bites — the bound-path and `dead` filters each drop **0** — so those two are shape guards holding a property, not measured reductions, and the block's own assertion is on *eligible > 0*, never on a filter biting.

The red and green samples differ in **exactly one status value** (plus the arithmetic the generated count artifact requires, so a stale count cannot mask the verdict), and "one value apart" is now checked as bytes by its own case rather than asserted in prose.

| leg | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **main** — tombstone + row `status: live` | exit **0** (green — the gate had no reading) | exit **1**, `<derived carrier> -> "live"`, with exactly one `✗` block in the output |
| **lit control** — same sample, legal status | exit 0 | exit **0** |
| **dark control** — ordinary non-tombstoned `live` rows | exit 0 | exit **0**, and the whole gate output is identical except the two lines added here |

The dark control is the strong form: a full diff of the gate's output on a legal ledger, before versus after, differs only by the new `tombstoned keys:` census line and the new clause in the summary sentence. All 39 per-type verdict lines and every other check's output are byte-identical, so nothing else was tightened.

The before-legs were taken by reverting both files to the base commit after the fix was committed, with the mutation proven on disk (blob hashes moved, the new symbols counted 0 occurrences) and the restore proven by `git diff HEAD` being empty and the blob hash matching `HEAD`'s.

## Non-vacuity

`0 forbidden` reads identically whether every row is honest or the marker drifted and the scan reached nothing, so the gate prints the population it asked on every run, pass or fail. On this PR's head `3d49d7a199` against the shipped ledgers (2026-09-18T22:08Z) it prints the green form:

```
tombstoned keys: 79 `[REMOVED]` tombstone(s) reached by the walk, 79 graded with a status the tombstone allows.
```

and on the red leg the same line carries the finding:

```
tombstoned keys: 79 `[REMOVED]` tombstone(s) reached by the walk, 78 graded with a status the tombstone allows, 1 FORBIDDEN.
```

and `orphans.test.ts` holds `TOMBSTONE_MARKER` equal to what `retiredKey()` actually writes, read from the producer rather than restated.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, measured rather than assumed. `@objectstack/spec`'s `files[]` is `dist · json-schema · liveness · prompts · llms.txt · README.md · src/**/*.zod.ts · CHANGELOG.md · api-surface · api-surface-declarations · spec-changes.json`; `scripts/` is not in it, and the build's entries are src modules. Each of the three symbols this PR adds occurs in **0** files under those shipped paths; positive controls through the same instrument and the same path set: `retiredKey` in 102, `ObjectSchema` in 30. Nothing this diff moves is shipped by any package.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed — observations, with no reproducible defect, contract violation or authoring trap behind them:

- PR #19059 landed `scripts/liveness/tombstoned-row-status.test.ts` as `a362e0e425` (2026-09-18T22:08Z), a contract test asserting the same invariant against the **real** ledgers at **top-level granularity only**. It is complementary rather than duplicative — that one pins today's ledgers in `Test Core`, this one is a gate rule over every depth the walk reaches and over any ledger root. Left untouched here, per triage's `⛔ 不折叠`. This PR is the second of the two, and both files were written without sight of the other.
- The gate's `markerStatus()` still has no `[REMOVED]` arm, deliberately: with a row present it is never consulted, and without one the UNCLASSIFIED failure is the louder answer. Recorded so the next reader does not read its absence as an oversight twice.
